variations.name: Scope 3 supplier data collection & engagement platforms
variations.description: Platforms that survey, score and coach thousands of suppliers to obtain primary emissions data and reduction commitments, attacking the 70-90% of a typical corporate footprint that sits in purchased goods and services.

companies.name: CDP
companies.what: The de facto global environmental disclosure system; its supply chain program lets buyers request standardized climate data from tens of thousands of suppliers.
companies.signal: Nonprofit operating 20+ years; referenced alongside EcoVadis/TfS as a default channel for supplier carbon data collection

companies.name: Manufacture 2030 (now Secaro)
companies.what: Facility-level supplier decarbonization program: measures plant emissions and drives implementation of reduction projects rather than just data collection.
companies.signal: Ford, GM, Toyota, Honda, Denso, Magna extending platform to ~20,000 supplier facilities (2024); 10 UK grocers (Tesco, Aldi, Sainsbury's) use it as decarbonization partner

companies.name: Sweep
companies.what: Paris-based sustainability data platform for collecting and centralizing scope 3 data from suppliers and distributed business units, CSRD-oriented.
companies.signal: Raised ~$100M total (Series B $73M, 2022, led by Coatue); positions as scope 3/value-chain leader

companies.name: Optera
companies.what: Boulder-based scope 1-3 emissions management with deep supplier-specific (vs spend-based) scope 3 modeling for enterprises.
companies.signal: $12M Series A (Sep 2023) led by Next Frontier Capital; founded from a sustainability consultancy

companies.name: Emitwise
companies.what: AI-driven supplier engagement that helped procurement teams get PCFs and SBTi targets from thousands of suppliers in minutes.
companies.signal: Acquired by Green Project Technologies (ACT Group) July 28, 2025; no longer a standalone brand — consolidation evidence in a crowded field

companies.name: SupplyShift
companies.what: Pioneer supplier sustainability network (founded 2012) with 100,000+ suppliers sharing assessment and scope 3 data with buyers.
companies.signal: Acquired by Sphera Jan 9, 2024 to bolt supplier data collection onto Sphera's LCA/ESG suite

companies.name: Green Project Technologies
companies.what: ACT Group-owned carbon data platform consolidating supply-chain climate tooling (absorbed Emitwise's supplier engagement and PCF tech).
companies.signal: Acquirer-of-record in 2025 scope 3 consolidation; backed by ACT Group, a major environmental commodities trader

companies.name: Avarni
companies.what: Sydney-based scope 3 data engine that ingests procurement spend and supplier data to map value-chain emissions; used by consultancies for client scope 3 work.
companies.signal: Active product releases through late 2025 targeting Australian ASRS mandatory climate reporting

variations.name: Supplier sustainability ratings & assessment networks
variations.description: Shared assessment networks rate a supplier's ESG and carbon performance once and reuse that rating across many buyers, making sustainability a standard, comparable procurement criterion at global scale.

companies.name: EcoVadis
companies.what: Category-defining shared supplier sustainability ratings (medals) used in procurement decisions, plus a Carbon Action Module with 48,000+ GHG reporters.
companies.signal: $500M raise (June 2022) at >$1B valuation led by Astorg/BeyondNetZero; 175,000+ rated companies in 180+ countries

companies.name: IntegrityNext
companies.what: Munich-based supplier ESG assessment and monitoring platform (25+ ready-made assessments) built for EU regulations like LkSG/CSDDD.
companies.signal: €100M from EQT Growth (Mar 2023) after bootstrapping; 200+ customers monitoring ~1M suppliers (Siemens Gamesa, Infineon, Hilti)

companies.name: Sedex
companies.what: Long-standing responsible-sourcing data network whose SMETA audit is the world's most-used social/environmental audit format.
companies.signal: Decades-old membership network spanning tens of thousands of buyer and supplier members

companies.name: Worldly
companies.what: Exclusive host of Cascale's Higg Index tools — facility- and product-level environmental data for apparel/consumer goods supply chains.
companies.signal: 40,000+ suppliers reporting on the platform; spun out of the Sustainable Apparel Coalition

companies.name: Assent
companies.what: Supplier ESG and product-compliance data network focused on complex manufacturing (electronics, aerospace, industrial).
companies.signal: $350M from Vista Equity (Jan 2022) at unicorn valuation; one of Canada's largest software raises

companies.name: Prewave
companies.what: Vienna-based AI that continuously monitors public signals on 140 risk types (ESG, deforestation, CBAM exposure) across n-tier supplier networks instead of relying on questionnaires.
companies.signal: €63M Series B (June 2024) led by Hedosophia; 200+ customers incl. Toyota, Ferrari, Lufthansa; 3x revenue growth 2023

variations.name: Product carbon footprinting & LCA software
variations.description: Software that models cradle-to-grave product footprints and EPDs, increasingly automated with AI and BOM/ERP integrations so manufacturers can footprint entire portfolios instead of commissioning one-off consultant studies.

companies.name: Sphera
companies.what: Owner of GaBi, the dominant enterprise LCA software and dataset franchise, now bundled with ESG risk and (via SupplyShift) supplier data collection.
companies.signal: Blackstone-owned ESG software consolidator; acquired SupplyShift Jan 2024 to add scope 3 collection to its LCA stack

companies.name: One Click LCA
companies.what: Construction-sector LCA/EPD market leader (BIM-integrated) expanding to all industries; now owns SimaPro, the classic expert LCA tool.
companies.signal: PSG Equity & InfraVia-backed; acquired SimaPro/PRé Sustainability (Sep 2, 2025), claiming world's largest LCA platform with 500,000+ datasets

companies.name: Makersite
companies.what: AI 'product digital twin' that auto-builds LCAs, cost and compliance models from BOMs across electronics, automotive and chemicals.
companies.signal: €60M Series B (summer 2025); ~50% growth since 2024; acquiring Siemens' SiGREEN (effective June 1, 2026)

companies.name: Carbonfact
companies.what: Apparel/footwear-specialized PCF platform using ML to footprint every SKU from incomplete product data.
companies.signal: $15M Series A (Apr 2024) led by Alven; 150+ brands incl. Columbia, New Balance, Carhartt

companies.name: Ecochain
companies.what: Amsterdam LCA platform (Mobius/Helix) for footprinting full product portfolios of mid-size manufacturers at once.
companies.signal: Ranked among top-5 LCA providers in 2025 vendor comparisons

companies.name: iPoint-systems
companies.what: German compliance-plus-LCA suite (Umberto) with 20+ years in automotive material compliance, adding supplier PCF outreach.
companies.signal: Named among LCA vendors investing in supplier engagement for primary data (2025-2026)

variations.name: Product carbon footprint data-exchange networks & standards infrastructure (PACT, Catena-X)
variations.description: Shared standards (PACT Pathfinder, Catena-X rulebooks) and conformant networks let verified product carbon footprints flow company-to-company across supply tiers, replacing industry-average estimates with primary data without exposing trade secrets.

companies.name: PACT (WBCSD)
companies.what: Neutral WBCSD-convened initiative defining the PCF methodology and technical data-exchange spec that vendor solutions certify against (PACT conformance).
companies.signal: Its framework is the alignment anchor for Catena-X, TfS and major vendors; growing ecosystem of conformant solutions

companies.name: Catena-X / Cofinity-X
companies.what: Automotive data ecosystem (BMW, Mercedes-Benz, Bosch, SAP, Siemens et al.) with a binding PCF Rulebook; Cofinity-X operates the live marketplace for standardized PCF exchange.
companies.signal: PCF Rulebook v3.0 published; first cross-OEM PCF exchanges live in European automotive and now extending to Asia

companies.name: SiGREEN (Siemens)
companies.what: Siemens-built PCF exchange that uniquely bridges TfS (chemicals), Catena-X and PACT; powers the TfS PCF Exchange for the global chemical industry.
companies.signal: PACT-conformant (2024); sold by Siemens to Makersite, deal effective June 1, 2026 — a signal that even industrial giants struggled to monetize exchange infrastructure standalone

companies.name: Glassdome
companies.what: US/Korean platform pulling real factory-floor sensor data into verified PCFs and exchanging them across borders without exposing raw process data.
companies.signal: $8.6M Series A (2023); ran Asia's first Catena-X-compliant PCF exchange with KG Mobility and LG Electronics (June 2026); works with Samsung SDI

companies.name: SAP (Sustainability Data Exchange)
companies.what: PACT-conformant PCF exchange embedded directly in the SAP procurement/ERP stack, giving it default distribution to most large manufacturers.
companies.signal: Live product within SAP's sustainability portfolio; leverages SAP's installed base rather than a new network

variations.white_space: Standards now exist but supplier-side adoption is the chicken-and-egg bottleneck: PCF exchange is consortium/nonprofit infrastructure with weak standalone monetization (Siemens divested SiGREEN). The opening is not another network but conformant exchange embedded in existing procurement/ERP rails and automated supplier-side PCF generation cheap enough for SME tiers 2-3.

variations.name: Food & agriculture supply chain emissions platforms
variations.description: Ingredient-level emissions databases and agricultural supply-chain MRV translate recipes and sourcing decisions into product footprints and farm-level interventions for food brands and retailers, where scope 3 is typically >90% of impact.

companies.name: HowGood
companies.what: World's largest food/personal-care sustainability database — 33,000+ ingredients, chemicals and materials — powering product-level impact scoring for CPGs and retailers.
companies.signal: $27.4M raised over 5 rounds (latest $12.5M, May 2022)

companies.name: CarbonCloud
companies.what: Swedish 'climate intelligence' engine that auto-calculates footprints for hundreds of thousands of food products and shares them via its ClimateHub network.
companies.signal: €7.5M Series A (Feb 2023); ~$14M total raised

companies.name: Carbon Maps
companies.what: Paris-based carbon/ESG platform built specifically for agricultural supply-chain complexity, mobilizing food suppliers for primary data and PCF validation.
companies.signal: ~€4M pre-seed (2023, Breega/Samaipata); growing in French/EU agrifood

companies.name: Planet FWD
companies.what: Decarbonization platform for consumer brands with deep food/agriculture LCA models (founded by Zume's Julia Collins).
companies.signal: $10M Series A (Acre, Congruent); ~$16.8M total raised; Morgan Stanley-profiled

companies.name: Mondra
companies.what: AI platform generating product-level LCAs from retailer specification data (thousands of LCAs in <4 hours); runs the BRC Mondra Coalition standardizing PCF across UK grocery.
companies.signal: Coalition with Tesco, M&S, Ocado, ASDA (Sainsbury's, Lidl, Co-op piloting), in consultation with WRAP/IGD/WWF-UK

companies.name: Regrow Ag
companies.what: Satellite + soil-model MRV that lets food companies verify regenerative practices and scope 3 reductions across sourcing regions (insetting).
companies.signal: $38M Series B (2022) led by Galvanize; General Mills monitoring 175M acres; Cargill and Kellogg's partnerships

variations.name: Freight & logistics emissions visibility and optimization
variations.description: Platforms calculate auditable per-shipment emissions across modes (GLEC framework / ISO 14083) and surface lower-carbon routing, modal-shift and consolidation choices, turning transport scope 3 from an annual estimate into an operational decision variable.

companies.name: project44
companies.what: Leading real-time transportation visibility platform that added GLEC-accredited Emissions Monitoring across all modes on top of its tracking network.
companies.signal: $2.7B valuation ($80M round led by Generation IM and A.P. Moller); Emissions Monitoring launched Aug 2024

companies.name: Shipzero
companies.what: Hamburg data platform creating primary-data emissions records (fuel-level) for road/sea/air freight shared between shippers and carriers.
companies.signal: €8M Series A (May 2024, ETF Partners); tracks 80M+ transports across 100+ countries

companies.name: Pledge
companies.what: London API/platform letting freight forwarders embed accredited emissions measurement and reporting into customer quotes and shipments.
companies.signal: $10M raise (2022, Zinal Growth) after $4.5M seed (Lowercarbon); Smart Freight Centre GLEC-accredited and ISO 14083-compliant

companies.name: Searoutes
companies.what: Marseille-based APIs computing vessel/route-specific CO2 per shipment so shippers can pick lower-emission carriers and routings.
companies.signal: ~$2.7M raised; niche but embedded in forwarder workflows

companies.name: EcoTransIT World
companies.what: The long-standing standard calculation engine for worldwide transport-chain emissions, accredited to GLEC/ISO 14083 and embedded in major carriers' and shippers' systems.
companies.signal: Operating since 2000s with broad industry adoption as the default freight-emissions calculator

companies.name: Convoy
companies.what: Digital freight network that marketed automated load-batching and empty-mile reduction as trucking decarbonization.
companies.signal: Raised ~$1.1B at a $3.8B peak valuation; ceased operations Oct 19, 2023 in the freight recession; tech sold to Flexport ($16M), then to DAT (2025)

variations.name: Green materials & low-carbon procurement marketplaces
variations.description: Databases and marketplaces that put EPD-backed carbon data next to price at the moment of specification and purchase, letting buyers choose low-carbon steel, cement, and other materials and converting Buy Clean-style policies into actual demand signals.

companies.name: Building Transparency (EC3)
companies.what: Hosts EC3, the only free, open-access global embodied-carbon calculator with a huge digitized EPD database used in material specification and procurement.
companies.signal: Nonprofit formed 2020; observes 30%+ carbon reductions where EC3 is used to procure; backbone of US Buy Clean implementation

companies.name: 2050 Materials
companies.what: London-based API/platform aggregating sustainability data on 150,000+ construction products so architects and contractors can compare and specify low-carbon options.
companies.signal: Accelerator-backed early-stage; largest open construction-materials sustainability database claim

companies.name: Vanilla Steel
companies.what: Berlin B2B digital marketplace auctioning European steel (surplus/excess prime), a digital channel relevant to sourcing lower-carbon and circular steel.
companies.signal: $4.1M raised (seed led by June Fund); building AI price/demand forecasting with EU co-funding

companies.name: Climate Earth
companies.what: Automated EPD generation for ready-mix concrete producers, feeding verified low-carbon concrete data into EC3 and procurement decisions.
companies.signal: EC3 ecosystem partner serving concrete producers across North America

companies.name: Skanska
companies.what: Global contractor that co-created EC3 (with Microsoft) and applies embodied-carbon-based procurement on major projects.
companies.signal: EC3 originated from Skanska's 2019 initiative; now industry-standard practice at scale

variations.white_space: Few transactional players because green premiums are uncertain, materials trade is regional and commoditized, and the best data infrastructure (EC3) is free and nonprofit — hard to monetize a standalone marketplace. The opening is the transaction layer: book-and-claim certificate systems and offtake aggregation for green steel/cement tied to Buy Clean and CBAM price signals, embedded into existing procurement/ERP and estimating software rather than new destinations.

variations.name: CBAM & carbon border compliance software
variations.description: Software that collects installation-level embedded-emissions data from non-EU producers and automates EU CBAM reporting and certificate cost forecasting — turning the world's first carbon border tariff (definitive phase from 2026) into a procurement data problem.

companies.name: CarbonChain
companies.what: Commodity-grade emissions accounting (metals, energy, agri) with a CBAM Supplier Catalogue — shared infrastructure for installation-level emissions data exchange between operators and EU importers.
companies.signal: Supports ~35% of steel, ~40% of aluminium and ~50% of fertiliser EU import volumes; 1,750+ declarations covering 7.5 Mt of goods over three years

companies.name: CBAMBOO
companies.what: London startup building the 'operating system for carbon border taxes' — importer exposure tracking plus free supplier-side tooling to generate compliant emissions data.
companies.signal: Founded May 2023 at Carbon13; Pale Blue Dot-backed; platform live for EU importers and non-EU manufacturers

companies.name: AEB
companies.what: Established German customs/global-trade software vendor integrating CBAM reporting into existing customs workflows via partnership with CBAMBOO.
companies.signal: Decades-old trade-compliance installed base; CBAM partner offering live

companies.name: Thomson Reuters (ONESOURCE)
companies.what: Global trade and tax compliance suite extending into CBAM declarations, giving multinationals CBAM inside the system that already files their customs entries.
companies.signal: Incumbent trade-compliance leader adding CBAM modules ahead of the 2026 definitive regime

variations.white_space: The Oct 2025 Omnibus simplification (50-tonne de minimis) exempted ~182,000 mostly-SME importers while keeping 99% of emissions in scope — gutting the long-tail SME software market but deepening enterprise and supplier-side need. Openings: tooling for non-EU producers (where default values now cost real money), integration into customs/ERP rails rather than standalone portals, and expansion to UK CBAM (2027) and other emerging border regimes.

variations.name: Deforestation-free supply chain (EUDR) monitoring & compliance
variations.description: Satellite monitoring plus supply-chain geodata platforms verify that cattle, cocoa, coffee, palm, rubber, soy and wood products weren't grown on deforested land and auto-file EU due-diligence statements — now mandatory for EU market access from 30 Dec 2026 after a one-year delay and simplification agreed in Dec 2025.

companies.name: osapiens
companies.what: Mannheim ESG-compliance HUB automating EUDR due diligence, traceability and TRACES reporting alongside CSDDD/CBAM modules.
companies.signal: $120M Series B (July 2024) led by Goldman Sachs Growth Equity; 1,300+ customers incl. Coca-Cola and Costco; 700+ users of its EUDR solution

companies.name: LiveEO
companies.what: Berlin satellite-analytics firm whose TradeAware product screens supplier plot geodata against AI deforestation detection for EUDR.
companies.signal: €25M Series B; demand spiked into the original 2024-2025 deadlines and again in 2025

companies.name: Satelligence
companies.what: Dutch satellite deforestation-monitoring specialist that can issue official due-diligence statements on clients' behalf — a workflow differentiator.
companies.signal: Used by Cargill and Unilever for commodity deforestation risk

companies.name: Sourcemap
companies.what: NYC supply-chain mapping pioneer covering the full EUDR workflow from farm-plot collection through deforestation screening to automated DDS submission to EU TRACES.
companies.signal: $47M raised total ($20M Series B, June 2023); 10+ years of deforestation-free supply chain mapping; clients incl. Oxford University Press

companies.name: Orbify
companies.what: Earth-observation app platform offering configurable EUDR monitoring solutions built on open satellite data.
companies.signal: Early-stage; publishes EUDR vendor landscape and ships EO compliance blueprints

companies.name: Global Forest Watch (WRI)
companies.what: Free, open satellite deforestation alert infrastructure (GLAD/RADD) that underpins much of the commercial EUDR tooling ecosystem.
companies.signal: De facto public data layer for forest monitoring globally

variations.name: Materials traceability platforms for batteries, metals & critical minerals
variations.description: Chain-of-custody platforms track batteries, metals and critical minerals from mine to finished product — increasingly carrying embedded CO2 data — to satisfy the EU Battery Regulation's digital battery passport (mandatory Feb 2027) and responsible-sourcing rules.

companies.name: Circulor
companies.what: First company to deploy battery passports at industrial scale, tracking raw materials, recycled content and CO2 end-to-end.
companies.signal: Powered the world's first EV battery passport on the Volvo EX90 (June 2024); 30 supply chains and 125+ facilities tracked; backed by Volvo and Jaguar Land Rover

companies.name: Minespider
companies.what: Blockchain-based mineral and battery passports (Open Battery Passport, May 2023) creating verifiable digital identities for raw material batches.
companies.signal: Integration trials with Microvast through 2024; Tata Elxsi collaboration (Jan 2025); named a top battery-passport company

companies.name: Circularise
companies.what: Dutch digital product passports using zero-knowledge proofs so suppliers can prove provenance/footprint without revealing confidential composition data.
companies.signal: Active in battery, plastics and metals value chains; EU DPP pilot ecosystem participant

companies.name: Optel Group
companies.what: Canadian traceability-technology incumbent (pharma serialization heritage) applying its supply chain tracking stack to batteries and critical materials.
companies.signal: Named among top companies in the battery passport market (projected $0.15B in 2025 to $2.35B by 2035, 32% CAGR)

companies.name: Everledger
companies.what: Blockchain provenance pioneer (diamonds, then batteries and critical minerals) — the sector's most prominent failure.
companies.signal: Raised $51.7M (incl. Tencent-led $20M Series A); entered administration April 2023 after a funding deal collapsed

companies.name: Glassdome
companies.what: Factory-floor-data PCF and digital carbon passports for the Korean battery/materials supply chain (Samsung SDI, L&F, Lotte aluminium chain).
companies.signal: $8.6M Series A with explicit EV-battery focus; organizer of a Global Battery Alliance passport pilot

variations.white_space: Voluntary provenance repeatedly failed to find a payer (Everledger insolvent 2023; IBM/Maersk shut their blockchain supply-chain products citing lack of collaboration) — the value accrued to regulators and consumers, not the companies paying for it. The EU Battery Regulation's mandatory passport (Feb 2027) plus US critical-minerals sourcing rules create the first hard compliance demand; the opening is audit-grade passports embedded in OEM PLM/procurement systems with CO2 data attached, not standalone blockchain networks.
